```{r setup}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmbk"))$meta$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12693>

Domagrozumab (PF-06252616) is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds
and neutralizes myostatin (growth differentiation factor 8, GDF8), a soluble
negative regulator of skeletal muscle growth. Tiwari 2020 fitted four
alternative population PK/PD models simultaneously to free domagrozumab and
total myostatin serum concentrations from the first-in-human study in healthy
adults, and compared them by fit and by the target coverage each predicts:

| Model | File | Drug elimination | Total myostatin |
|---|---|---|---|
| QSS | `Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_qss` | linear + complex internalization (QSS binding, `Kss`) | synthesis, degradation, drug-bound fraction cleared at `kint` |
| MM-BK (selected) | `Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmbk` | linear + Michaelis-Menten (`Vmax`, `Km`) | as QSS, but binding does not feed back on the PK |
| MM-IDR2 | `Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmidr2` | as MM-BK | indirect response, drug inhibits degradation (`Imax`, `IC50`, Hill) |
| MM-IDR3 | `Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmidr3` | as MM-BK | indirect response, drug stimulates synthesis (`Smax`, `SC50`, Hill) |

The four models are independent fits with their own parameter estimates
(Table 1), so each is a separate model file. The authors carried the MM-BK
model forward because it balanced fit, mechanism and the precision of its
target-coverage predictions, even though MM-IDR2 had the lowest objective
function value.

```{r models}
mod_names <- c(
  QSS = "Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_qss",
  `MM-BK` = "Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmbk",
  `MM-IDR2` = "Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmidr2",
  `MM-IDR3` = "Tiwari_2020_domagrozumab_mmidr3"
)
mods <- lapply(mod_names, function(nm) rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(nm)))
mods_typ <- lapply(mods, rxode2::zeroRe)
# Every model has the same four ODE states in the same order, so the
# event tables below address them consistently.
stopifnot(all(vapply(
  mods,
  function(m) identical(m$state, c("depot", "central", "peripheral1", "total_target")),
  logical(1)
)))
```

# Population

The data come from a Phase 1, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled
dose-escalation study in healthy adults (Tiwari 2020 Methods, "Clinical study,
PK, and myostatin data"): single IV doses of 1, 3, 10, 20 and 40 mg/kg infused
over 2 hours, a single SC dose of 3 mg/kg, and a repeat-dose cohort of 10
mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for 3 doses. Tiwari 2020 defers subject numbers and
demographics to the study report (Bhattacharya 2017, Clin Pharmacol Drug Dev
7:484-497), so the number of subjects is not given in the model metadata.
The lower limits of quantification were 0.2 nM for free domagrozumab and 0.04
nM for total myostatin; 21 domagrozumab and 1 myostatin observation were
dropped from the analysis (Supplement, Figure S3).

# Source trace

All parameter values are from Tiwari 2020 Table 1 (one column per model). The
in-file comments in each model give the column, value and RSE.

| Element | Source location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| QSS drug equation | Eq. 1, Eq. 5 | central holds total drug; free drug from the QSS root |
| Depot and peripheral equations | Eqs. 2-3 | shared by all four models |
| QSS / MM-BK total myostatin | Eqs. 4 and 7 | identical in both models |
| MM-BK, MM-IDR drug equation | Eq. 6 | linear + Michaelis-Menten elimination |
| MM-IDR2 total myostatin | Eq. 8 | `ksyn - kdeg (1 - Imax DC^g / (IC50^g + DC^g)) Mtot` |
| MM-IDR3 total myostatin | Eq. 9 | `ksyn (1 + Smax DC^g / (SC50^g + DC^g)) - kdeg Mtot` |
| `ksyn = kdeg M0` | Methods, QSS model paragraph | baseline homeostasis |
| `k12 = Q/VC`, `k21 = Q/VP`, `kel = CL/VC` | Methods, QSS model paragraph | |
| Target coverage, MM-BK | Eq. 10 | also applied to the QSS model (same myostatin equation) |
| Target coverage, MM-IDR2 | Eq. 11 | not defined for MM-IDR3 |
| CL, VC, Q, VP, ka, Fbio | Table 1, PK parameters | per kg (mL/h/kg, mL/kg) |
| Kss, kint, kdeg, M0 | Table 1, PD parameters | |
| Vmax, Km | Table 1, PD parameters | Vmax in nmol/h/kg |
| IC50/SC50, Imax/Smax, gamma | Table 1, PD parameters | IDR models only |
| IIV (CL, VC, M0, kint, vmax, IC50/SC50, Imax/Smax) | Table 1, random variability; Supplement "Population Model" | log-normal, CV% converted as `log(1 + CV^2)` |
| Residual error | Table 1 RUV; Supplement "Population Model" | exponential (log-additive) for drug, proportional for myostatin |
| Molecular weight of domagrozumab, 150,000 g/mol | not in Tiwari 2020; Nguyen 2020 Table 2 | needed for mg to nmol |

# Virtual cohort

Doses in the study were given per kilogram and every structural PK parameter
is reported per kilogram, so with a dose of (mg/kg x body weight) all
concentrations are independent of body weight. The cohorts below therefore
use a fixed 70 kg body weight for the healthy-adult cohorts and 30 kg for the
pediatric regimen of Figure 5; the weight only sets the mg amount.

```{r cohort-helpers}
# Phase 1 cohorts of Tiwari 2020: dose (mg/kg), route, number of doses and
# dosing interval (h). The infusion lasts 2 hours.
cohorts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,              ~dose_mgkg, ~route, ~n_dose, ~ii,
  "1 mg/kg IV",                     1, "IV",         1,   0,
  "3 mg/kg IV",                     3, "IV",         1,   0,
  "10 mg/kg IV",                   10, "IV",         1,   0,
  "20 mg/kg IV",                   20, "IV",         1,   0,
  "40 mg/kg IV",                   40, "IV",         1,   0,
  "3 mg/kg SC",                     3, "SC",         1,   0,
  "10 mg/kg repeat IV",            10, "IV",         3, 336
)
cohort_levels <- cohorts$treatment

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120,
  seq(168, 60 * 168, by = 84)
)))

# One subject's records for a regimen given as a data frame of dose times,
# per-kg amounts and routes. Observation rows name the central state and
# carry dvid = 1 so that rxode2 returns every endpoint of these
# two-endpoint models.
make_subject <- function(id, wt, dose_df, obs) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id,
    time = dose_df$time,
    amt = dose_df$dose_mgkg * wt,
    dur = ifelse(dose_df$route == "IV", 2, NA_real_),
    cmt = ifelse(dose_df$route == "IV", "central", "depot"),
    evid = 1L,
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  observations <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_,
    cmt = "central", evid = 0L, dvid = 1L
  )
  out <- rbind(doses, observations)
  out$WT <- wt
  out[order(out$time, -out$evid), ]
}

cohort_doses <- function(row) {
  data.frame(
    time = (seq_len(row$n_dose) - 1) * row$ii,
    dose_mgkg = row$dose_mgkg,
    route = row$route
  )
}

make_cohort_events <- function(n_per_cohort, wt = 70) {
  out <- list()
  next_id <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cohorts))) {
    ids <- next_id + seq_len(n_per_cohort)
    next_id <- max(ids)
    ev_i <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ids, make_subject,
      wt = wt, dose_df = cohort_doses(cohorts[i, ]), obs = obs_times
    ))
    ev_i$treatment <- cohorts$treatment[i]
    out[[i]] <- ev_i
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}

# Typical-value solves (zeroRe() models) run one subject per cohort; rxode2
# warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega, which is intended here.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}

solve_cohorts <- function(model, events, label) {
  sim <- withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(model, events, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
  sim$model <- label
  sim
}
```

# Typical-value predictions by cohort

## Free domagrozumab (Figure 2 and Figure S2)

```{r typical-solve}
ev_typ <- make_cohort_events(n_per_cohort = 1)
typ <- bind_rows(lapply(names(mods_typ), function(nm) {
  solve_cohorts(mods_typ[[nm]], ev_typ, nm)
})) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = cohort_levels),
    model = factor(model, levels = names(mod_names)),
    week = time / 168
  )
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 7}
typ |>
  filter(Cc > 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, Cc, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (weeks)",
    y = "Free domagrozumab (nM)",
    colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Population predictions of free domagrozumab",
    caption = "Replicates the PRED curves of Figures 2 and S2 of Tiwari 2020; dashed line = LLOQ 0.2 nM."
  )
```

The QSS model clears domagrozumab almost linearly: its only nonlinear route is
the internalization of the drug-myostatin complex, which is limited by the
small myostatin pool (about 0.15-0.7 nM). The three models with a
Michaelis-Menten term bend down once free drug falls below `Km` (about 10 nM),
which is the late nonlinear decline the paper credits to the MM-BK model. The
three MM models share almost identical PK estimates, so their curves overlap,
as in Figure S2.

```{r fig2-check}
# Time at which the typical free-drug profile falls below the LLOQ, per
# model and single-dose cohort (weeks).
t_lloq <- typ |>
  filter(treatment != "10 mg/kg repeat IV", time > 24) |>
  group_by(model, treatment) |>
  summarise(week_below_lloq = min(week[Cc < 0.2]), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = week_below_lloq)
knitr::kable(t_lloq, digits = 1, caption = "Weeks until the typical free domagrozumab concentration falls below 0.2 nM.")

# The Michaelis-Menten models reach the LLOQ sooner than the QSS model at the
# lowest dose: the nonlinear decline the paper describes for Figure 2b.
low <- t_lloq[t_lloq$treatment == "1 mg/kg IV", ]
stopifnot(low[["MM-BK"]] < low[["QSS"]])
```

The MM-BK curves reach the LLOQ about 1.5-2.5 weeks earlier than the PRED
curves of Figure 2b. The late decline below `Km` is governed by
`CL + Vmax/Km`, and Table 1 prints Vmax to one significant figure (0.002
nmol/h/kg, so anything from 0.0015 to 0.0025). The table below brackets that
rounding: the crossing times digitized from Figure 2b by the maintainers sit
at the 0.0015 end of the bracket. The packaged model keeps the printed 0.002.

```{r fig2-vmax-rounding}
sd_rows <- cohorts[cohorts$n_dose == 1, ]
fine_obs <- seq(24, 60 * 168, by = 12)
ev_fine <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sd_rows)), function(i) {
  ev_i <- make_subject(i, wt = 70, dose_df = cohort_doses(sd_rows[i, ]), obs = fine_obs)
  ev_i$treatment <- sd_rows$treatment[i]
  ev_i
}))

crossing_weeks <- function(vmax) {
  m <- rxode2::ini(mods_typ[["MM-BK"]], lvmax = log(vmax))
  solve_cohorts(m, ev_fine, "MM-BK") |>
    group_by(treatment) |>
    summarise(week = min(time[Cc < 0.2]) / 168, .groups = "drop")
}

vmax_bracket <- crossing_weeks(0.0025) |>
  dplyr::rename(vmax_0.0025 = week) |>
  left_join(crossing_weeks(0.002) |> dplyr::rename(vmax_0.002 = week), by = "treatment") |>
  left_join(crossing_weeks(0.0015) |> dplyr::rename(vmax_0.0015 = week), by = "treatment") |>
  left_join(
    # Weeks at which the MM-BK PRED curve crosses the 0.2 nM LLOQ line,
    # digitized from Figure 2b (reading error about 0.5 week).
    tibble::tibble(
      treatment = c("1 mg/kg IV", "3 mg/kg IV", "10 mg/kg IV", "20 mg/kg IV", "40 mg/kg IV", "3 mg/kg SC"),
      figure_2b = c(16.8, 22.2, 27.1, 30.1, 34.3, 20.0)
    ),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = cohort_levels)) |>
  arrange(treatment)

vmax_bracket |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Cohort = treatment,
    `Vmax 0.0025` = vmax_0.0025,
    `Vmax 0.002 (packaged)` = vmax_0.002,
    `Vmax 0.0015` = vmax_0.0015,
    `Figure 2b` = figure_2b
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Weeks until the typical MM-BK free domagrozumab concentration falls below 0.2 nM, for Vmax across its rounding interval, against Figure 2b.")

# Every digitized crossing lies inside the rounding bracket, widened by the
# 1-week digitizing and grid allowance.
stopifnot(
  all(vmax_bracket$figure_2b > vmax_bracket$vmax_0.0025 - 1),
  all(vmax_bracket$figure_2b < vmax_bracket$vmax_0.0015 + 1)
)
```

## Total myostatin (Figure 3 and Figure S1)

```{r fig3, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(typ, aes(week, Myo, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (weeks)",
    y = "Total myostatin (nM)",
    colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Population predictions of total myostatin",
    caption = "Replicates the PRED curves of Figures 3 and S1 of Tiwari 2020."
  )
```

```{r fig3-check}
myo_peak <- typ |>
  group_by(model, treatment) |>
  summarise(peak_nM = max(Myo), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = peak_nM)
knitr::kable(myo_peak, digits = 2, caption = "Peak typical total myostatin (nM).")

# MM-BK plateaus (Figure 3a: about 0.7-0.8 nM at 10-40 mg/kg), while
# MM-IDR2 keeps rising with dose (Figure 3b: about 0.9 nM at 40 mg/kg);
# the paper attributes this to the sublinear Hill coefficient.
bk <- setNames(myo_peak[["MM-BK"]], myo_peak$treatment)
idr2 <- setNames(myo_peak[["MM-IDR2"]], myo_peak$treatment)
stopifnot(
  abs(bk[["40 mg/kg IV"]] - bk[["10 mg/kg IV"]]) / bk[["10 mg/kg IV"]] < 0.10,
  idr2[["40 mg/kg IV"]] > 1.1 * idr2[["10 mg/kg IV"]],
  # Baseline total myostatin equals M0 for every model.
  all(abs(typ$Myo[typ$time == 0] - c(0.141, 0.149, 0.144, 0.145)[as.integer(typ$model[typ$time == 0])]) < 1e-6)
)
```

# Stochastic predictions of total myostatin (Figure 4)

```{r fig4-solve}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200101)
ev_vpc <- make_cohort_events(n_per_cohort = 100)
vpc <- bind_rows(
  solve_cohorts(mods[["MM-BK"]], ev_vpc, "MM-BK"),
  solve_cohorts(mods[["MM-IDR2"]], ev_vpc, "MM-IDR2")
) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = cohort_levels), week = time / 168)

vpc_sum <- vpc |>
  group_by(model, treatment, week) |>
  summarise(
    p025 = quantile(Myo, 0.025),
    p50 = median(Myo),
    p975 = quantile(Myo, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig4, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(week)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p025, ymax = p975, fill = model), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50, colour = model)) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (weeks)",
    y = "Total myostatin (nM)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Simulated total myostatin: median and 95% interval",
    caption = paste(
      "Compare with Figure 4 of Tiwari 2020 (100 simulated subjects per cohort,",
      "individual predictions without residual error)."
    )
  )
```

# Target coverage in the pediatric DMD regimen (Figure 5)

Figure 5 simulates the regimen tested in boys with Duchenne muscular
dystrophy with the healthy-adult MM-BK and MM-IDR2 models: 5 mg/kg every 4
weeks for 16 weeks, then 20 mg/kg every 4 weeks for 16 weeks, then 40 mg/kg
every 4 weeks for 16 weeks, all as 2-hour IV infusions.

```{r fig5-solve}
dmd_doses <- data.frame(
  time = (0:11) * 672,
  dose_mgkg = rep(c(5, 20, 40), each = 4),
  route = "IV"
)
dmd_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48 * 168, by = 12), (1:12) * 672 - 0.01)))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200102)
ev_dmd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:200, make_subject,
  wt = 30, dose_df = dmd_doses, obs = dmd_obs
))
ev_dmd$treatment <- "DMD regimen"
ev_dmd_typ <- make_subject(1, wt = 30, dose_df = dmd_doses, obs = dmd_obs)
ev_dmd_typ$treatment <- "DMD regimen"

mw_drug <- 150000 # g/mol, domagrozumab (Nguyen 2020 Table 2)
mw_myo <- 25000 # g/mol, mature myostatin (Nguyen 2020 Table 1)

dmd <- bind_rows(
  solve_cohorts(mods[["MM-BK"]], ev_dmd, "MM-BK"),
  solve_cohorts(mods[["MM-IDR2"]], ev_dmd, "MM-IDR2")
) |>
  mutate(
    week = time / 168,
    conc_ugmL = Cc * mw_drug / 1e6,
    myo_ngmL = Myo * mw_myo / 1000
  )
dmd_typ <- bind_rows(
  solve_cohorts(mods_typ[["MM-BK"]], ev_dmd_typ, "MM-BK"),
  solve_cohorts(mods_typ[["MM-IDR2"]], ev_dmd_typ, "MM-IDR2")
) |>
  mutate(week = time / 168)

dmd_sum <- dmd |>
  select(model, week, conc_ugmL, coverage, myo_ngmL) |>
  pivot_longer(c(conc_ugmL, coverage, myo_ngmL), names_to = "output") |>
  group_by(model, output, week) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(value, 0.05),
    p50 = median(value),
    p95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(output = factor(output,
    levels = c("conc_ugmL", "coverage", "myo_ngmL"),
    labels = c("Domagrozumab (ug/mL)", "GDF8 coverage (%)", "Total GDF8 (ng/mL)")
  ))
```

```{r fig5, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(dmd_sum, aes(week)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "darkred", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(output ~ model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = NULL,
    title = "Simulated PK, target coverage and total myostatin",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 5 of Tiwari 2020: median (dashed) and 5th-95th",
      "percentiles of 200 simulated subjects per model."
    )
  )
```

The Results state that the MM-BK model predicts serum target coverage from
90% after 4 weeks to nearly 100% after 48 weeks, and the MM-IDR2 model only
from 40% after 4 weeks to about 80% after 48 weeks.

```{r fig5-check}
cov_at <- function(df, mdl, t) df$coverage[df$model == mdl & abs(df$time - t) < 1e-6]
coverage_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Model = c("MM-BK", "MM-BK", "MM-IDR2", "MM-IDR2"),
  Time = c("Week 4 (trough)", "Week 48", "Week 4 (trough)", "Week 48"),
  `Tiwari 2020 (%)` = c(90, 100, 40, 80),
  `Typical value (%)` = c(
    cov_at(dmd_typ, "MM-BK", 672 - 0.01), cov_at(dmd_typ, "MM-BK", 48 * 168),
    cov_at(dmd_typ, "MM-IDR2", 672 - 0.01), cov_at(dmd_typ, "MM-IDR2", 48 * 168)
  )
)
knitr::kable(coverage_tab, digits = 1, caption = "Target coverage: paper text against the typical-value simulation.")
stopifnot(abs(coverage_tab$`Typical value (%)` - coverage_tab$`Tiwari 2020 (%)`) < 5)

# First 5 mg/kg infusion: end-of-infusion concentration close to dose / VC
# (5 mg/kg / 46 mL/kg = 108.7 ug/mL), as in Figure 5a,b.
peak_typ <- dmd_typ |>
  filter(time == 2) |>
  mutate(conc_ugmL = Cc * mw_drug / 1e6)
stopifnot(all(abs(peak_typ$conc_ugmL / (5 / 46 * 1000) - 1) < 0.05))
```

# Mathematical equivalence of MM-BK and MM-IDR2 (Discussion)

The Discussion notes that, with Hill coefficient 1, the myostatin equation of
the QSS / MM-BK models equals the MM-IDR2 equation with `Imax = 1 - kint/kdeg`
and `IC50 = Kss`, which gives `Imax = 0.8` and `IC50 = 4.39 nM` from the
MM-BK estimates.

```{r equivalence}
bk_ini <- setNames(mods[["MM-BK"]]$iniDf$est, mods[["MM-BK"]]$iniDf$name)
imax_equiv <- 1 - exp(bk_ini[["lkint"]]) / exp(bk_ini[["lkdeg"]])
stopifnot(abs(imax_equiv - 0.80) < 0.01, abs(exp(bk_ini[["lkss"]]) - 4.39) < 1e-8)

# Numerically: an MM-IDR2 solve with those values and Hill = 1 reproduces the
# MM-BK total myostatin for the same drug profile.
idr2_equiv <- mods_typ[["MM-IDR2"]] |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lcl = log(0.102), lvc = log(46), lq = log(0.326), lvp = log(33),
    lka = log(0.009), lfdepot = log(0.73), lvmax = log(0.002), lkm = log(10.1),
    lkdeg = log(0.046), lrbase = log(0.149),
    limax = log(imax_equiv), lic50 = log(4.39), lhill = log(1)
  )
eq_bk <- solve_cohorts(mods_typ[["MM-BK"]], ev_typ, "MM-BK")
eq_idr <- solve_cohorts(idr2_equiv, ev_typ, "MM-IDR2 (equivalent)")
stopifnot(max(abs(eq_idr$Myo - eq_bk$Myo)) < 1e-4)
```

# PKNCA of the single-dose cohorts

Tiwari 2020 does not report NCA results (they are in the study report,
Bhattacharya 2017), so the table below characterizes the simulated cohorts
without a published comparator. The dose-normalized exposure rising with dose
is the nonlinear PK the Michaelis-Menten models were built to capture.

```{r pknca}
sd_cohorts <- c("1 mg/kg IV", "3 mg/kg IV", "10 mg/kg IV", "20 mg/kg IV", "40 mg/kg IV", "3 mg/kg SC")
nca_conc <- vpc |>
  filter(model == "MM-BK", treatment %in% sd_cohorts, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

nca_dose <- ev_vpc |>
  filter(evid == 1, treatment %in% sd_cohorts) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  left_join(cohorts |> select(treatment, dose_mgkg), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(
    auc_per_dose = aucinf.obs / (dose_mgkg * 70),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = sd_cohorts)
  ) |>
  arrange(treatment) |>
  select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, auc_per_dose, half.life) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Cohort = treatment,
    `Cmax (nM)` = cmax,
    `Tmax (h)` = tmax,
    `AUC0-inf (nM*h)` = aucinf.obs,
    `AUC0-inf / dose (nM*h/mg)` = auc_per_dose,
    `t1/2 (h)` = half.life
  )
knitr::kable(nca_tab, digits = 2, caption = "Median NCA parameters of the simulated MM-BK cohorts (100 subjects per cohort).")

iv <- nca_tab[grepl("IV", nca_tab$Cohort), ]
stopifnot(
  # Dose-normalized AUC rises with dose (nonlinear elimination saturates).
  iv$`AUC0-inf / dose (nM*h/mg)`[iv$Cohort == "40 mg/kg IV"] >
    1.2 * iv$`AUC0-inf / dose (nM*h/mg)`[iv$Cohort == "1 mg/kg IV"]
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Molecular weight.** Tiwari 2020 reports doses in mg/kg and concentrations
  in nM but does not print the molecular weight used for the conversion. The
  models use 150,000 g/mol, the domagrozumab value in Nguyen 2020 (Table 2).
  The figures support it: the 5 mg/kg end-of-infusion concentration in
  Figure 5a (about 110 ug/mL) matches dose / VC.
* **Units of Vmax.** Table 1 gives Vmax in nmol/hour/kg, an amount rate per
  kilogram, although Eq. 6 is written in concentration form. The models apply
  Vmax as an amount rate (Vmax x WT x C / (Km + C)). Read as a concentration
  rate, the Michaelis-Menten clearance would be about 20-fold smaller than
  the linear clearance and could not produce the nonlinear decline of
  Figure 2b; the amount reading reproduces it and the Figure 5 coverage.
* **Rounding of Vmax.** Table 1 prints Vmax as 0.002 nmol/h/kg in all three
  Michaelis-Menten models. The packaged models use that value; the late PK
  decline then runs 1.5-2.5 weeks ahead of the Figure 2b population
  predictions, which a Vmax near 0.0015 (still printed as 0.002) reproduces.
  The value was not adjusted.
* **Body weight.** WT is not a covariate in the paper. It converts the
  per-kilogram parameters to per-subject values so that doses are supplied in
  mg; concentrations do not depend on it.
* **IIV on VC, not VP.** Table 1 and the Results list IIV on CL, VC, M0
  (and kint, vmax, IC50/SC50, Imax/Smax). The Supplement "Population Model"
  paragraph names VP instead of VC; the models follow Table 1.
* **CV% conversion.** The paper does not define its IIV CV%; the variances
  are `log(1 + CV^2)`. No IIV correlations are reported, so the etas are
  independent.
* **Residual error.** Free domagrozumab was modelled on the log scale with
  additive error (exponential error), encoded as `lnorm(expSd)` with the
  reported 18-26% as the log-scale SD. Total myostatin uses a proportional
  error.
* **Target coverage.** Coverage (Eq. 10) and free myostatin are computed as
  model outputs for QSS and MM-BK, and with Eq. 11 for MM-IDR2. The paper
  defines no coverage for MM-IDR3.
* **Figure 5 population.** The paper simulated the pediatric DMD regimen with
  the healthy-adult models and their variability (500 subjects). This
  vignette uses 200 subjects per model and plots individual predictions
  without residual error, so the 5th-95th percentile bands are comparable to
  the paper's only approximately. The figures of total myostatin in ng/mL use
  25,000 g/mol for mature myostatin (Nguyen 2020 Table 1).
* **Numerical guard.** In the IDR models the free-drug concentration in the
  Hill term is floored at 0, because a fractional power of a tiny negative
  solver value is not a number. This does not change any solution.
